pubDate: "2026-06-15"

Joel once spent four months with a tax-return tab open in his browser, minimised, never clicked. He earned enough. The admin wasn't complicated. But the tab stayed shut because opening it meant the number inside would become real.

That is not laziness. It is a very ordinary form of avoidance that shows up in people who are otherwise capable and organised in every other part of their lives.

If you earn well and still feel a low hum of dread when your banking app sends a notification, the question worth sitting with is not "why am I so bad with money." The more honest question is: what do you think you're going to see, and what would it mean about you if you saw it?

That question is where the real work starts.

Joel works with earners who have the income but not the relationship with it. If that sounds familiar, the [money scripts quiz](/quiz) takes under three minutes and gives you a specific place to look, not a generic pep talk.
